decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm pickup approach, lifting and orienting toward the charger; left arm remains home.
Continue gradual elbow-up right wrist rotation and raised approach, adapting yaw to the visible charger.
Finish most of the pickup tilt while staying above the charger; wrist view will guide final centering.
Complete pickup tilt and lower partway toward the charger, keeping fingers open and checking centering.
Lower gently and correct the wrist yaw so the open fingers align with the charger sides; grasp not yet confirmed.
Fine-center the charger between the open fingers and descend the final centimeter before closing.
Close the right gripper around the centered charger; retention will be checked during a small lift.
Lift the closed right gripper to verify charger retention before moving toward the central handoff.
Charger appears retained in the lifted gripper. Begin turning it toward a central, non-crossing handoff while raising clearance.
Continue the raised right-arm turn toward the handoff; charger remains visually steady between the fingers.
Move the retained charger toward the right side of the central handoff while smoothly continuing its yaw rotation.
Continue the central handoff approach, holding the charger closed and preserving the right-arm configuration.
Finish orienting the held charger at the central handoff and begin the left arm's raised, open-gripper approach.
Keep the charger steady at the handoff while advancing the left arm upward and forward with an open gripper.
Advance the left gripper toward the held charger at clearance height, continuing its smooth inward-facing rotation.
Bring the left open gripper closer to the charger handoff, easing downward only after reaching clearance.
Align the left gripper with the charger's free end, approaching slowly while the right maintains its grasp.
Approach the free charger end with the left fingers open, using the wrist view for the final handoff alignment.
Fine approach to the charger free end; raise the left wrist slightly to center its grip while the right holds still.
Close the left gripper on the free charger end while keeping the right grip closed for a supported handoff.
Hold the left grip closed and gently release the right gripper, then inspect whether the charger stays supported.
Separate the hands slowly after releasing the right gripper; check that the charger moves with the closed left gripper.
The charger slipped during handoff. Open and separate both hands to regain a clear view for recovery.
Recover directly with the left arm: tilt its open gripper downward toward the charger's free end and descend at a controlled rate.
Move the left open gripper closer over the fallen charger, keeping its wrist on the left side and increasing the downward approach angle.
Refine the left-arm recovery approach, bringing its open fingers down and forward around the charger body.
Close the left fingers around the recovered charger and begin a small lift to test retention.
Lift the recovered charger clear of the table with the left gripper closed, checking that it follows the hand.
Charger is moving with the left hand. Raise it clear and begin turning its prongs downward toward the strip orientation.
Carry the charger leftward at clearance while choosing the equivalent socket orientation that keeps the arm comfortably bent.
Continue carrying left and turning the held charger with small continuous wrist increments, keeping it above the strip.
Continue the upright-plug rotation and shift left at clearance height; keep the recovered charger clamped.
Continue gradual orientation toward downward prongs, keeping clearance and monitoring the left wrist configuration.
Use the equivalent socket yaw in the opposite direction to avoid winding the left wrist near its limit; raise and reposition at clearance.
Continue unwinding toward the equivalent insertion yaw and reposition the left wrist over the near end of the strip at safe height.
Continue the socket-facing rotation while lowering partway from clearance; keep the left-arm elbow-up configuration continuous.
Ease toward the nearer socket with smaller position and rotation increments, maintaining clearance while completing the upright orientation.
Replan from the interrupted pose: pause rotation and move slightly lower and back to relieve the wrist configuration while keeping the charger clear.
Use a very small first correction to bridge the accepted-target tracking difference, then gently relieve the left wrist without rotating.
Complete the downward-prong tilt in small increments while moving back and lower to keep the left wrist away from its limit.
Pause the rotation and retract the held charger toward the robot to relieve the tightly folded wrist before final alignment.
Resume the downward-prong orientation with small increments while lowering toward a better-conditioned approach height.
Back away from the strip and finish the upright tilt at a less folded arm posture; the charger remains clamped.
Finish matching the socket yaw and upright tilt before translating toward it; keep the prongs above the tabletop.
Translate the upright charger toward the near socket with small increments, monitoring the folded wrist and keeping a clearance margin.
Withdraw leftward and back from the constrained approach; preserve the grasp while making room for the other equivalent socket orientation.
Turn toward the opposite socket-facing yaw while withdrawing left and back, keeping the charger safely clamped and above the table.
Continue the smooth yaw turn while moving the left wrist back toward a comfortable insertion approach; charger remains retained.
Continue rotating the held charger toward the opposite equivalent socket yaw while shifting the left wrist back and left.
Keep the charger elevated and continue the gradual socket-yaw turn with the left elbow remaining up.
Slow the yaw rotation through the wrist transition, retaining the charger and maintaining clearance.
Continue the controlled yaw turn and back-left positioning toward the strip, keeping the charger clear of the surface.
Bring the upright charger nearer to the strip's middle socket while continuing the equivalent yaw alignment at clearance.
Ease the held charger into the final socket-facing yaw while keeping the left wrist behind the strip and the prongs elevated.
Finish the socket yaw alignment and shift slightly left over the middle socket before lowering the prongs.
Lower the upright charger cautiously toward the middle socket, keeping the left grip closed and watching alignment.
Advance the prongs only a few millimeters, monitoring the socket alignment and any visible resistance.
Back off slightly from contact and make a small lateral correction to center the two prongs on the socket slots.
Make a final tiny lateral correction, then test a shallow insertion while holding the charger upright.
The two prongs appear aligned with the slot pair; lower a further few millimeters without lateral motion.
The charger appears resisted rather than fully seated. Lift slightly and correct a few millimeters toward the near side of the slot pair.
Fine-center the visible prongs on the outer slot pair, then test a shallow downward insertion without forcing a large motion.
The prong tips now visually coincide with the slots. Continue a slow straight insertion and check whether the exposed pin length decreases.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating for any motion: gently lift, then shift the prongs forward toward the slot centers.
Test the corrected slot alignment with a slow six-millimeter descent, watching for reduced exposed prong length.
Continue a slow straight insertion from the corrected alignment, checking that the socket covers more of each prong.
Relieve contact and correct the remaining lateral offset of the right prong before another shallow seating test.
Correct the rejected tensor from the unchanged pose: lift clear of contact, then shift forward across the socket face.
Test the new depth alignment with a slow straight descent, checking whether the slots cover the pins rather than pushing the charger out of the grip.
Continue a very small straight seating motion at the aligned slot pair, watching for pin coverage and any charger slip.
The charger is slipping instead of seating. Lift clear of the lip and move the pin pair farther across the socket face before retrying.
Lower only partway toward contact while adjusting the right wrist for an additional view of the socket; both arms remain on their own sides.
Approach the slot plane slowly and improve the side view with the right wrist to check the charger's depth alignment.
The side view suggests the charger is beyond the socket centerline. Relieve contact and shift back across the strip before retesting.
Use the side view to approach the remaining vertical gap, with a tiny lateral correction and slow straight descent.
Relieve the blocked insertion and shift the charger back across the socket face; repeated contact has changed its position within the grip.
Shift slightly farther toward the near side of the socket and test contact again with a controlled vertical descent.
Continue straight down in small increments at the newly centered position, checking both wrist views for actual pin entry.
Back clear of the resistant lip, then move the pin pair farther across the strip face; verify alignment from the side view before seating.
Lower from clearance at the new cross-strip position, using the visible pin and slot spacing to check for entry.
Close the remaining visible vertical gap with small straight steps, monitoring both views for contact or actual seating.
Release the charger onto the strip and back the low grip away. Inspect its support and seating before attempting a safer higher grasp.
